body.title: Understand changes before committing
body.problem: Developers can commit completed designs and implementations without knowing whether they understand the behavior, decisions, and failure modes they are accepting. Existing delivery approvals and reviews describe the work, not a particular person's understanding, so uncertainty and confident misconceptions are invisible. There is no contextual assessment of the proposed commit's impact, no proportional understanding requirement, and no durable record connecting a person's demonstrated knowledge or explicit exception to the exact changes committed.

summary.prose: Before a commit, developers receive an understanding check proportionate to its contextual impact. They can learn through guided explanations, demonstrate understanding, and retain a personal record without changing the work item's completion status. High-impact exceptions are explicit and visible in the commit message.

nonGoals.text: Changing work-item approvals or completion status
nonGoals.rationale: Individual understanding and delivery status are separate.

nonGoals.text: Standalone Grokcheck runtime, Python service, or external browser product
nonGoals.rationale: The daemon owns the lifecycle; VS Code is the initial surface.

nonGoals.text: New agent adapters, additional IDEs, video courses, or spaced repetition
nonGoals.rationale: Defer expansion until the core pre-commit flow works.

assumptions.text: The current specification and mocks express the desired product behavior; unresolved implementation choices require explicit decisions before implementation.

constraints.text: Daemon owns canonical state, keys, grading, guidance, and authorization; clients use IPC only.
Impact classification is contextual daemon reasoning, never line-count or filename rules.
Trivial skips; Low optional; strict Medium requires completion regardless of result; configured High requires pass or explicit commit-recorded override.
Assessment and authorization bind to the intended staged snapshot and base; changed content cannot reuse authorization silently.
Unsure immediately starts guidance; incorrect submitted answers also start guidance; reading guidance alone is not a pass.
Preserve personal original answers, confidence and assisted attempts separately from work-item delivery state.
Use existing CLI-backed providers with sequential LLM calls and daemon-served structured context, never direct cloud REST.
Copy/adapt relevant pinned Grokcheck modules with attribution; no separate Grokcheck process or Python runtime.
Assessments appear in a resumable VS Code editor pane; UI scores cannot authorize commits.

stories.title: Keep a personal, resumable understanding record
stories.userValue: I can resume my check and distinguish my understanding from delivery progress.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a developer begins a check for a staged change
acceptanceCriteria.when: the session is saved and later resumed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the same person's answers, confidence, assisted attempts and progress remain associated with the original change and linked work items

acceptanceCriteria.given: a linked epic, story, task or issue is completed
acceptanceCriteria.when: a check is failed, skipped or resumed
acceptanceCriteria.then: its delivery status and approvals remain unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.given: the editor closes or the daemon restarts during a check
acceptanceCriteria.then: persisted progress is recoverable and missing or uncertain state cannot masquerade as a pass

functionalRequirements.statement: Retain personal understanding history and resumable progress independently of delivery state.

stories.title: Explain change impact and the applicable project requirement
stories.userValue: I understand why this commit needs a check and what the project requires.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an exact staged change and its base are available
acceptanceCriteria.then: the daemon provides High, Medium, Low or Trivial with contextual reasons and relevant evidence rather than a filename or line-count rule

acceptanceCriteria.given: a classification and current project settings exist
acceptanceCriteria.then: Trivial bypasses assessment, Low offers a voluntary check, strict Medium requires completion without score blocking, and enabled High requires a pass or explicit override

acceptanceCriteria.given: context or classification is unavailable or uncertain
acceptanceCriteria.then: the user sees the uncertainty and recovery options without silently treating it as Trivial or a pass

functionalRequirements.statement: Classify staged change impact contextually and explain the resulting project requirement.

stories.title: Demonstrate understanding with grounded questions
stories.userValue: I can demonstrate understanding of the actual requirements, design and behavior I am committing.

acceptanceCriteria.given: linked requirements, design, implementation, tests and review evidence are available
acceptanceCriteria.then: questions address the exact change and cite supporting evidence; unavailable evidence is disclosed rather than invented

acceptanceCriteria.given: a developer submits an answer and confidence
acceptanceCriteria.then: the daemon records the first response and determines the outcome using validated criteria; the editor cannot declare itself passed

acceptanceCriteria.given: an assessment is run with any supported authoring assistant
acceptanceCriteria.then: the same daemon-managed experience works without requiring Claude-specific hooks or a separate Grokcheck service

functionalRequirements.statement: Provide evidence-grounded questions and authoritative evaluation for the staged change.

stories.title: Learn through guidance after uncertainty or an incorrect answer
stories.userValue: I can understand the concept I missed and demonstrate what I learned.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a question is visible with no answer submitted
acceptanceCriteria.then: guided understanding opens immediately with explanation and relevant evidence

acceptanceCriteria.given: an answer has been submitted
acceptanceCriteria.then: the user receives a guided walkthrough of the concept and supporting evidence

acceptanceCriteria.given: the user has read guidance
acceptanceCriteria.then: a fresh grounded question assesses understanding; reading guidance alone never yields a pass and the original attempt remains visible separately from assisted outcomes

functionalRequirements.statement: Provide immediate contextual guidance and fresh reassessment while preserving original and assisted outcomes.

stories.title: Complete and resume checks in a VS Code editor pane
stories.userValue: I can manage the whole check alongside my code without leaving VS Code.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a commit needs or offers a check
acceptanceCriteria.then: an editor pane shows impact, rationale, requirement, linked scope and progress with questions, confidence, guidance and results

acceptanceCriteria.given: the pane is closed or reloaded
acceptanceCriteria.then: the daemon's current session and eligibility are shown without losing saved answers or granting permission from stale UI state

acceptanceCriteria.given: a check is offered voluntarily or requires an override
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user chooses skip or override
acceptanceCriteria.then: the pane clearly distinguishes voluntary decline from a recorded exception and explains the commit consequence

functionalRequirements.statement: Expose the full check and recovery experience in a resumable VS Code editor pane.

stories.title: Apply proportional checks to the exact commit
stories.userValue: I can commit once the applicable requirement is satisfied, knowing the decision covers what is actually committed.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a commit is attempted under enabled policy
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pre-commit check evaluates current evidence
acceptanceCriteria.then: Trivial proceeds without a test, Low may decline, strict Medium proceeds after completion regardless of outcome, and enabled High passes automatically only after a successful test

acceptanceCriteria.given: a previously checked snapshot or base changes
acceptanceCriteria.then: old passes and overrides no longer authorize the new commit while historical results are retained

acceptanceCriteria.given: the daemon is unavailable or concurrent attempts occur
acceptanceCriteria.when: a required check cannot be confirmed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the user receives actionable recovery and the commit is not silently authorized with an unknown result

functionalRequirements.statement: Authorize only the intended staged commit according to the current project requirement and valid evidence.

stories.title: Explicitly override a High requirement with a durable commit record
stories.userValue: I can make an accountable exception when I cannot pass or choose to skip a High check.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an enabled High check is failed or skipped
acceptanceCriteria.when: the developer does not explicitly override
acceptanceCriteria.then: the commit remains blocked

acceptanceCriteria.given: an enabled High check is failed or skipped
acceptanceCriteria.when: the developer explicitly confirms an override for the current snapshot
acceptanceCriteria.then: the exception and reason are recorded in the actual resulting commit message and understanding history

acceptanceCriteria.given: the required override record is missing from the final message or the staged content changes
acceptanceCriteria.then: the exception cannot authorize that commit

acceptanceCriteria.given: a valid High assessment succeeds
acceptanceCriteria.then: it proceeds automatically without requiring an override

functionalRequirements.statement: Require explicit, snapshot-specific exceptions for failed or skipped High checks and preserve the exception in the final commit message.

requirements.statement: Commit requirements vary with contextually classified impact and project policy.
The person receives evidence-backed assessments and guided help when unsure or incorrect.
Understanding history is attributable to a person and exact work version without altering delivery status.
Only matching current evidence and explicit user decisions can authorize the intended commit.
Retain personal understanding history and resumable progress independently of delivery state.
Classify staged change impact contextually and explain the resulting project requirement.
Provide evidence-grounded questions and authoritative evaluation for the staged change.
Provide immediate contextual guidance and fresh reassessment while preserving original and assisted outcomes.
Expose the full check and recovery experience in a resumable VS Code editor pane.
Authorize only the intended staged commit according to the current project requirement and valid evidence.
Require explicit, snapshot-specific exceptions for failed or skipped High checks and preserve the exception in the final commit message.
